notes:
Overview: LocaleFlux is a contact-center platform serving retail and travel verticals across NA/EU/LATAM. Primary pain: inconsistent tone+translations across locales and high escalation rates for non-English tickets. They run multi-tenant Zendesk + proprietary agent desktop.

Customer wants: agent-assist that: suggests localized replies, performs instant ticket summarization in agent language, calls internal tools (lookup order/status) securely, and provides regional routing when capacity spikes. Emphasis on deterministic fallbacks in case of degraded model capacity.

Quotes / call snippets:
- 'Must sound local — not literal translations. Tone varies by market (formal FR, friendly BR-PT).' — Head of CX
- 'Black Friday season is our make-or-break — need predictable latency and graceful degradation.' — VP Eng

Integration notes: existing systems to integrate: Zendesk (webhooks), internal order API (OAuth2), SSO via Okta, KMS provider: AWS KMS, SIEM: Splunk. Data residency requirement: EU PII must stay in EU region for EU customers; some global customers require on-prem pockets.

POC goals: 1) demonstrate 95th percentile latency < 350ms for short agent prompts under 200 RPS; 2) translation/tone quality score > 0.85 on internal eval set; 3) safe tool-calling (rate-limited, audit logged) with zero PII leaks in 5000 sample requests.

Risks called out: potential quality regression when aggressively quantizing multi-lingual models; network complexity for hybrid private deployments; timing on legal approval for residency appendix.
requirements_summary:
- Workloads: prompt-completion agent assist (short prompts), ticket summarization (longer context), embeddings for similarity search, on-demand translation microservice.
- Latency/throughput: target p95 < 350ms for < 200 token assistant responses under normal load; sustain 2x traffic during peak (holiday sales) with graceful fallback to smaller model and degraded feature set.
- Model preferences: multilingual open models preferred, ability to pin model families and fallback to quantized variants.
- Routing: locale-based regional routing + capacity-tier fallback (dedicated -> hosted).
- Security: SSO, KMS integration, audit trails for tool invocations, EU data residency and export controls.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and alerting for translation quality drift.
technical_acceptance_criteria: Latency: p95 < 350ms for 90% of test slices (agent prompts) during steady state
Quality: translation/tone MOS >= 4.2 / 5 on sampled human evals
Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model with < 1% error rate when primary pool saturated
Security: end-to-end audit logging for tool calls, KMS-encrypted keys in transit and at rest
Integration: runbook for Zendesk webhook + OAuth order lookup; zero PII exfiltration in 5k test requests
poc_plan: Week 0: Access + onboarding - provide test tenants, SSO test account, and sample transcripts
Week 1: Smoke tests - deploy dedicated pool (2 nodes), wire Zendesk staging, validate tool-calling flow
Week 2: Stress & quality - run spike tests (2x expected), run translation/human evals, compare quantized vs float models
Week 3: Harden & handoff - finalize residency config, deliver acceptance report, legal sign-off support
